title: Subprime Lender Goeasy Sees Elevated Writeoffs Before Business Improves
content: Subprime lender Goeasy Ltd., which surprised investors weeks ago with a surge of bad debts in its vehicle financing business, said it expects loan writeoffs to remain elevated for a while before getting better later in the year.

title: Brazil’s Braskem Said to Plan Court Protection Against Creditors
content: Braskem SA, Brazil’s largest petrochemical company, is considering seeking protection in local courts against its creditors, according to people involved in the talks.

title: Why Carson Block Is Placing Bearish Bets on Credit ETFs
content: Carson Block, founder and CEO of Muddy Waters Research, explains his bearish outlook on credit markets, highlighting expectations for credit spreads to widen significantly. He speaks during an interview on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Carson Block Lays Out Bearish Credit ETF Bets Amid AI Fears
content: Famed short seller Carson Block is placing bearish bets on some of the biggest corporate credit ETFs as a way to hedge the risk of economic malaise caused by AI.

title: Lenders to Vista's Software Firm Solera Form Pact as Loans Near Maturity
content: A group of senior lenders to Solera Holdings Inc., including Apollo Global Management Inc. and Pacific Investment Management Co., has tapped a legal adviser ahead of the software company’s debt maturing in 2028, according to people familiar with the situation.

title: Carson Block Warns About AI, Talks ETFs and Credit Spreads
content: Muddy Waters Capital founder and CEO Carson Block says investors are underestimating the risk AI poses to the labor market and US economy. Speaking on "Bloomberg The Close," Block also comments on credit spreads and where he is finding investment opportunities. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Crypto Get Easier Path to 401(k)s
content: Bloomberg's Loukia Gyftopoulou, joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." Companies offering alternative assets in retirement savings plans would get more legal protection under a new Trump administration proposal. The changes could make it easier for 401(k) plans to include private credit, private equity, crypto and real estate investments. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Petro’s ‘Worst Mistake’ Saves Colombia Central Bank From Turkey’s Fate
content: Colombian President Gustavo Petro says that naming Olga Lucía Acosta to the central bank was his biggest blunder, after she resisted his calls to slash interest rates. For the same reason, others credit her with saving the bank’s independence and the nation’s inflation-targeting model.

title: US Banks’ Private-Credit Zeal Fuels $348 Billion Pile of Loans
content: Wall Street has been pouring into private credit, fueling rapid growth in firms’ portfolios of loans to non-banks.

title: Fintech Funding Jumped 27% In 2025 With Fewer Deals But Bigger Checks
content: Global venture funding to fintech startups climbed in 2025 to its highest level in several quarters, boosted by later-stage deals, Crunchbase data shows.

title: The Largest Recent Seed Rounds Are All For AI Companies
content: A majority of top seed funding recipients in the past six months operate at the intersection of AI and the physical world. Using Crunchbase data, we take a look at some of the sector's biggest seed rounds in recent months.

title: Seed Funding Hasn’t Stalled, But It’s Skewing Larger And Is More Competitive Than Ever, Crunchbase Data Shows
content: Among U.S. seed funding deals, it’s only the upper bands of larger and outlier seed rounds — those $10 million and above — that grew in 2025, Crunchbase data shows.

title: Fed holds interest rates steady — here’s what that means for consumers
content: From mortgage rates to auto loans and credit cards, here’s a look at how the Fed's March interest rate decision may affect your finances.

title: Private credit's cracks open door for Wall Street banks' comeback: 'The tug of war is just starting'
content: Wall Street banks may finally be getting a long-awaited opening to claw back market share from private credit lenders.

title: Moody's cuts rating on private credit fund run by KKR and Future Standard to junk as bad loans grow
content: The move by Moody's is the latest sign of distress in private credit; retail investors have been rushing to withdraw funds, from Blackstone to Apollo.

title: Apollo gives investors only 45% of requested withdrawals from $15 billion private credit fund
content: The withdrawals show that Apollo didn't avoid the rush of investor redemptions plaguing rivals, driven by concern over private credit loans to software firms.

title: Credit card APRs have an 'economically meaningful' impact on consumer spending, Boston Fed finds
content: When credit card rates go up, borrowers spend less on plastic, according to a research paper by the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston.

title: More than 7 million student loan borrowers face deadline to leave Biden-era repayment plan. What to know
content: Student loan borrowers will be removed from the Saving on a Valuable Education, or SAVE, plan, later this year, Trump officials said.

title: As March Madness unfolds, NY Fed highlights sports betting toll on consumer credit health
content: As sports gambling becomes more popular and less restricted, consumer credit health is suffering, according to a new report by the New York Fed.

title: More than 7 million student loan borrowers are in a defunct payment plan — what that means for their money
content: Here's what student loan borrowers should know about the consequences of remaining in the SAVE forbearance — and what their other options are.

title: When it comes to private credit, 'some caution is reasonable,' advisor says. What to know
content: While there are pockets of weakness in private credit, concern about a broad-based meltdown among these funds may be misplaced, some experts say.

title: Trump admin tasks Treasury Dept. with student loan collection. What borrowers need to know
content: Trump officials plan to task the Treasury Department with collecting on defaulted student loans and eventually "operational support" on current loans.
